prompt: Give every constant of the TextRule enum its own body implementing the abstract apply method, then chain the rules together with applyAll.
explanation: Declaring apply abstract forces every constant to supply a body, and each body is really an anonymous subclass of the enum -- so TextRule.TRIM and TextRule.STRIP_VOWELS are different classes sharing one type. That gives you polymorphism without a switch: applyAll just loops and calls apply, and adding a fifth rule needs no change there. Note that the rules are not commutative, which is why applyAll feeds each result into the next rule rather than applying them all to the original text.
hints: Each constant body goes between braces after the constant name, and the shared abstract apply declaration sits after the semicolon that ends the constant list.
TRIM and COLLAPSE_SPACES are one-liners (trim(), and replaceAll(" +", " ")); the other two are easiest with a StringBuilder and a character loop.
For TITLE_CASE the test `i == 0 || input.charAt(i - 1) == ' '` decides whether to upper-case; applyAll keeps a `String result` variable and reassigns it inside the loop.
